meta.what: The feature matrix: each layer of a macOS 27 guest on x86, what runs there today, and how far the 27-only goal is.

states.done: 27's own piece (or a piece that needs no 27 replacement) is in place and was seen working in at least one boot
states.in progress: a stand-in from macOS 26 is still used, or 27's piece runs with a known wall

evidence_levels.measured: seen in a boot or a test, n says how many

rows.today: Stock QEMU with KVM on Linux, unmodified
rows.note: Nothing to change in QEMU so far.

rows.today: OVMF (UEFI), as shipped by the OSX-KVM project
OpenCore 1.0.x with the project's own configuration
rows.note: Its custom kernel-slide setting is needed: without it Apple's boot.efi sometimes picks a slide that lands in firmware-reserved memory (9 of 9 boots passed with it).

rows.part: APFS driver for the boot loader
rows.today: macOS 26's apfs.efi
rows.note: 27's APFS container carries no x86 EFI driver.

rows.today: macOS 26's x86 boot.efi (27.0.1 ships no x86 boot loader), edited on disk so it creates two device-tree properties 27's userland expects from firmware
rows.note: Without them, kmutil and kextload abort about 11 s after start; with them they run.

rows.today: From Apple's Kernel Debug Kit, with seven early-boot patches and a set that maps the commpage into user processes
rows.note: Apple still ships an x86_64 kernel in 27.0.1's KDK, but on this guest it does not boot as shipped: several early-boot paths assume arm64 behaviour.

rows.today: Built from Apple's published xnu source (xnu-12377.121.6, macOS 26.5) plus 27's missing interfaces, now at the project's version 1.5.4
rows.n: 4 boots to loginwindow on the hybrid; 3 boots of the 27-only root at 1.5.4
rows.note: Not Apple's kernel: its version string is 25.5.0. It needs none of the load-time patches. Missing syscalls, MIG routines and exports were re-derived from 27's own x86_64 machine code; closed routines with no source were re-emitted from 27's machine code and checked instruction by instruction. Not matching Apple yet, found on 2026-11-25 (1 run each): a process running as an ordinary user set its own task's kernel port to null, and this kernel allowed it, with the guest's security settings (which allow unrestricted NVRAM and an unauthenticated root, but not a kernel debugger); afterwards the kernel's call that names the process's own task answered null. On an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 27.0.1, Apple's arm64 kernel, with System Integrity Protection on, refused the same call (KERN_NO_ACCESS); the two machines' security settings differ, so that comparison is not like for like. A reading of Apple's published xnu source, which this kernel is built from, allows the call only when the kernel-debugger setting is on, which the guest's settings leave off. Why this kernel allows it is not read.

rows.today: 66 minutes beside Apple's kernel on the same disk
rows.note: 0 panics either way, the same crash reports at the same rate. Not repeated on 1.5.x.

rows.part: DEVELOPMENT build of the self-built kernel
rows.today: Boots, then core daemons end themselves in a loop
rows.note: Both boots were on an earlier version of the kernel and have not been repeated on 1.5.x. In the first, 2,304 daemon exits in 26 minutes against 1 on RELEASE on the same host; in the second, a boot argument that allows the legacy message trap did not stop them. The RELEASE build compared did not show the loop; the cause is not found.

rows.today: A Rosetta-shaped exec option in the self-built kernel: the arm64e program is the process, and a static x86_64 runtime beside it runs a translator
rows.note: The kernel answers Apple's own identity, code-directory hash and entitlements for the translated program. Off unless a boot argument turns it on.

rows.today: 185 of 27's own x86_64 kexts, 9 borrowed from macOS 26, the recompiled Sandbox kext, and the kernel
rows.note: Full list: docs/kexts.md, for the collection the furthest earlier root booted with. A collection with one more entry, Apple's x86_64 IOUserSerial.kext from 27.0.1's Kernel Debug Kit, clears the registry stall (docs/gaps.md, B18): 4 test boots first, and it is in the project's default test bases since 2026-11-24 (2 test boots each).

rows.today: macOS 26's kmutil, run inside a recovery guest
rows.note: 27's own kmutil runs under translation in the guest, but has not yet loaded a kext or built a collection there.

rows.today: 27.0.1's own arm64e Sandbox.kext, the 958 reachable functions of its 967 recompiled to x86_64 and wrapped by a generated adapter
rows.n: 2 boots on Apple's kernel image; on the self-built kernel, 2 boots agreeing on every probe row plus 1 on a later version
rows.note: Enforces read, write, exec, network and default-deny as native 27.0.1 does. The network-outbound probe rows are no reading, and a named-sysctl deny is consistent with enforcement but not closed.

rows.part: Platform kexts with no 27 x86_64 build
rows.today: ACPI platform set, APIC, EFI runtime and NVRAM, HPET, bus power controller: borrowed from macOS 26
rows.note: The route that recompiled the Sandbox kext is the planned replacement.

rows.today: Borrowed from macOS 26
rows.note: 27.0.1's KDK does have an x86_64 build, so this one is a swap, not a recompile.

rows.today: 27's own x86_64 dyld and x86_64 shared cache (the one Apple ships for Rosetta)
rows.note: The main cache is signed with 16 KiB hash pages, which the x86 kernel rejected, so it is re-signed at 4 KiB. The cache's own signature is ad hoc, so nothing is lost.

rows.today: 27.0.1's own APFS system volume, in a real volume group with a Data volume seeded from 27's template
rows.note: Placed files were checked against the placement records, with ten deliberate damages all caught.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e launchd and xpcproxy, recompiled to x86_64
rows.note: Since 2026-11-24 the project's default test bases, each one standalone disk image, carry both (2 test boots each; the one adopted on 2026-11-25 is built from the first). Stopping a service no longer takes the guest down: an earlier build of the recompiled launchd exited when it stopped a service, and the kernel panicked (1 control boot). With the fix, 0 panics in 2 boots; in one of them launchd waited its 10 s exit timeout, then killed a service that ignored the stop request, and stayed pid 1 throughout. xpcproxy relinked with the newer link tools binds lazily loaded libraries as dyld does: before, the two launchd jobs that name a cryptex (accountsd and spindump) never started, 428 failed spawns in one boot; with it, both ran in each of the 6 boots that reached a login with it. Details per program: docs/boot-programs.md.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e boot tasks, recompiled to x86_64
rows.note: The boot reaches the daemon phase with them in place. Success was read for some tasks only (docs/boot-programs.md says which); xpcroleaccountd's outcome is unread.

rows.today: On the furthest root, in the boot the note counts, by label: 299 labels (289 programs) of 27's own x86_64 programs, 110 labels (105 programs) of programs 27.0.1 ships without an x86_64 slice, under translation, 7 recompiled, 3 borrowed from macOS 26 (amfid, logd, logd_helper), and 2 whose file flags were changed. In three later boots 27's own replaced the three borrowed ones
rows.note: One boot of about 1,000 s: launchd's job table held 411 labels; 126 of them showed a process id or an exit status, 15 of those a nonzero one. Counting only labels whose program is on 27's system volume or, for five under /Library/Apple, in its Data-volume template, 118 of 388 ran (one of the five among them). docs/launchd-labels.md lists 421 such labels: the 388, plus 33 that are in 27's launchd plists but were not in that boot's job table. These counts are of labels, not programs: a program can serve more than one label. They were taken before 27's own amfid, logd and logd_helper replaced macOS 26's. Full list: docs/launchd-labels.md.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e logd and logd_helper under translation on the furthest configuration
rows.note: Both run with exit status 0 in 3 of 3 boots, where macOS 26's builds ran before; in one boot the kernel's code-directory hashes for both equal Apple's arm64e builds. 27's own log command reading back a message sent through 27's logd was measured on other configurations, 2 of 2, not yet on this one.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e amfid under translation
rows.note: It stays up, exit status 0, in 4 boots, where macOS 26's crashes in every boot. In one boot it refused an ad hoc signed test program carrying a restricted entitlement, with Apple's own error for that case. A test with an edited signature did not discriminate, so validation is only partly tested.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e sandboxd under translation
rows.note: Died at boot when launchd started it, before patch X. With X, a hand-started copy got past the failure in 2 of 2 boots; in the second, the launchd-started copy was still restarting, though it ran with a trace option the hand-started one did not, so the two are not a controlled comparison. That fix (patch X) had an open race and has been replaced by patch Y, whose boots are not written up in this record yet.

rows.today: 27's own kernelmanagerd under translation
rows.note: Starts and checks in. The 240-second registry stall it reported is explained (docs/gaps.md, B18): with either measured fix, 0 stall lines in every test boot counted. The project's default test bases since 2026-11-24 carry one of the fixes.

rows.today: Apple's own virtio network driver on QEMU's legacy virtio device
rows.note: Chosen as a device shape with no edit to 27. Without a fix for the registry stall (docs/gaps.md, B18), it attaches only after that stall.

rows.today: Apple's configd gets an address by DHCP
rows.note: Late: at about 320 to 370 s of uptime.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e sshd under translation, started by a test payload in debug mode
rows.n: 3 of 3 logins in 8 of 9 boots with a 180 s timeout, 1 of 3 in one
rows.note: launchd's own sshd job worked on another root over loopback; host logins to it on this configuration are not measured. With a 60 s connect timeout, logins failed: 0 in each of 2 boots of this configuration, and 0 in each of 5 consecutive boots of another test series. The cause is the login harness's own time budget, read from its logs: first banners took 24 to 56 s against the 60 s timeout, each try was capped at 150 s, and the debug sshd serves one connection, so later tries met no listener. A boot of that series with a 180 s timeout logged in 2 times, which is consistent with that explanation (n = 1). With 180 s on this configuration, 8 of 9 boots logged in 3 of 3 and one 1 of 3. First logins took up to 239.73 s from connect to the end of the login session, in the boot that logged in once.

rows.today: 27's x86_64 SkyLight with QuartzCore's software compositor
rows.note: Draws the recovery window, Disk Utility and the installer. Two small byte edits on disk work around a display-state field that 27's x86_64 encoder and arm64e decoder disagree on, and a place where 27's code assumes a Metal compositor; no debugger is needed.

rows.today: 27's own arm64e WindowServer under translation. With the hybrid image's two display byte edits placed in this root's cache, it stays up, shows the boot progress window, and then 27's login window
rows.n: several boots of overlays of the 27-only root
rows.note: In the boot this row first recorded, it never opened the framebuffer, and its last display line said Apple's display manager is unsupported. With those edits in the root's cache it stays up and shows the boot progress window. The login window then appeared in 2 of 2 boots of one set-up and 1 of 2 of another when nothing held the display awake, and in each of 11 later boots in which a login was typed: whether it appears looks like a race with the guest's display going to sleep, and once the display sleeps nothing redraws it (inferred from one boot's timing, in which SecurityAgent logged that it was showing its window one second before the screens slept) (docs/gaps.md, B21). Render-fence timeouts in its log were checked in one boot and are not the wall.

rows.today: No Metal device. A software Vulkan driver (lavapipe) loads in the guest and runs a compute shader correctly
rows.note: 4,096 of 4,096 values correct, byte-identical to lavapipe on Linux. Not connected to Metal.

rows.today: 27's own loginwindow under translation draws the login window and takes a typed login; the user session starts and the first-login User Account Updater completes; with Setup Assistant skipped by a per-user marker the test places, the Dock, Finder, SystemUIServer and Control Center start and stay up, the Dock is drawn about half an hour after the login, and in one boot a menu bar and a wallpaper were drawn and a click opened the Apple menu; WindowManager keeps crashing
rows.n: login window and typed login: 11 boots; user session: 9; User Account Updater: 6; Dock, Finder, SystemUIServer and Control Center started: 4; Dock drawn: 3 of 4; menu bar, wallpaper and the click: 1
rows.note: On test overlays of the 27-only root, which are not yet the default test base. The translator fix for mapping short shared-memory objects (docs/translator-patches.md, Q2) got the login past its audit step, so the session started; later, xpcproxy relinked so that accountsd could start let User Account Updater finish (docs/boot-programs.md). In the 2 boots in which the first-login Setup Assistant then ran, no pane of it appeared (in the first it was seen to become the frontmost app), the screen stayed black, and no Dock or Finder process started; why is not read. With a per-user marker that skips Setup Assistant, the four session programs start within about 1 to 6 minutes of the login and stay up (4 boots), and the Dock is drawn between about 20 and 35 minutes after the login (3 of 4 boots). In the first completed login boot with the translator fix for app-sandboxed programs (docs/translator-patches.md, AA), a menu bar and a wallpaper were drawn for the first time on the 27-only root, and a click on the Apple menu was seen to open it (1 boot). In that boot WindowManager crashed and was restarted all through it (in the boot before, it stayed up from its tenth start), and no Finder window has been drawn (docs/gaps.md, B22 and B25). A recompiled build of loginwindow exits with status 70 each time (1 boot, 236 starts); the cause is not read.

rows.today: Version 0.5.6; refuses by name any instruction form it does not handle
rows.note: 0 functions refused in every binary tried. Closing battery: 8,939 operand forms, 572,096 cases against the Unicorn emulator.

rows.today: Runs each recompiled function and Apple's arm64e original under emulation from the same state
rows.note: launchd 1,403 pass, 0 fail, 65 no reading; xpcproxy 99, 0, 1. A pass requires two deliberate-bug controls to be caught.

rows.today: Bind every import of a recompiled program by name to Apple's x86_64 library build; C, Swift and Objective-C calls converted
rows.note: Nothing of libSystem, libxpc, libdispatch, libobjc or the Swift runtime is translated. Newer versions also convert Objective-C aggregates and lazily loaded libraries: a recompiled daemon that died about every 10 s at a lazy-load helper ran the whole boot after relinking (70 such deaths to 0), the recompiled diskarbitrationd served both disk rounds, and a relinked xpcproxy let the two launchd jobs that name a cryptex start (1 boot each).

rows.today: Version 0.17.0; turns lifted kext functions into one loadable x86_64 kext
rows.note: All 225 C++ virtual-call sites dispatched by method.

rows.today: Checks a lifted kext function against the original with generated input specs
rows.note: 79 of 119 pass, 0 fail; the rest refused or no reading. 79 of the Sandbox kext's 967 functions are verified this way; the rest only by what the kext does in a boot.

rows.today: The open-source Maclator translator with a local patch stack, kept on a public branch of the project's fork
rows.n: see docs/translator-patches.md; the default test bases: 2 test boots each
rows.note: Changes that fit upstream are still offered there as small changes. Pull request #12 (patch G) was merged on 2026-11-10; on 2026-11-23, pull requests #16 (patch K), #17, #18, #19 and #22 and two questions as issues (#20 and #21) were posted, all open at this snapshot (UPSTREAMS.md). The project's default test base adopted on 2026-11-24 ran the build with the shared-memory mapping fix (Q2) as its default translator: in its 2 test boots every required row passed (24 of 24 and 22 of 22). The one that replaced it on 2026-11-25 runs a later build, adding the one root-owned store of slid data (R2) and the guest-memory fix (Z): in its 2 test boots every required row passed (31 of 31 and 29 of 29). In both, amfid still runs an older build, and recompiled programs are not translated. Those changes and later ones (AA among them), with internal comments removed, are public on the fork's branch queue/boot-tested-2026-11-24 (UPSTREAMS.md); the translator built from that branch's tip has not itself been booted (local builds carrying R2, Z and AA have).

rows.part: Mutation tests of the tools' self-tests
rows.today: For 31 of the project's internal tools and scripts (binary analysis, image building and boot drivers), a table of deliberate bugs; each bug is put into a copy of the tool, and the tool's self-test must then fail on the control named for it
rows.note: All 603 were caught in one run on a frozen tree (2026-11-22). This shows that those self-test controls can fail; it does not show that the tools are free of other bugs. The lifter is not among the 31.
